## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The discourse concludes with an inspired utterance (*udāna*) [Shaw 2006].

Curated parallels include a nearly verbatim Pali parallel in the *Navakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 9.3) and a Chinese parallel in the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 56). DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these relationships, identifying massive Pali-internal text reuse with AN 9 (122 matches, covering §1.2–17.1_1 with §3.1.1–3.15.2 at 0.91 similarity) and automatic alignment with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26, best score 65) [DharmaNexus]. Resembling verse parallels are preserved in the *Cittavarga* chapters of various *Udānavarga* recensions (UV 31, UVS 31, Uv Kg 31, T 212, and T 213). DharmaNexus also traces widespread text reuse across the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10, AN 5, AN 8, AN 6), *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 45, SN 46, SN 35), and later commentaries such as the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* and *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
